key_insight: Permeability in brittle rocks under dynamic loading is governed primarily by how crack geometry evolves—especially crack length, opening, and connectivity—rather than by porosity alone.
engineering_relevance: This matters for predicting fluid flow in reservoirs, containment systems, and other geological formations subjected to fast loading or stress changes.
method: Model rock void space as an evolving network of penny-shaped cracks with prescribed orientations.
Update permeability from crack microvariables: aperture, length, and crack spacing/distance.
Include opening/closure, propagation, nucleation, coalescence, and strain-rate-dependent fracture toughening in the evolution law.
evidence_signal: Implemented in the GeoDyn hydrocode and tested under tension, shear, compression, and symmetric impact, the model reproduced permeability changes spanning several orders of magnitude across stress states and loading rates.
watch_item: Predicted permeability can be strongly limited by poor crack connectivity or crack closure, so accurate orientation and connectivity inputs are critical for reliable use.
paper_title: Permeability and microcrack geometry: Dynamic loading induced evolution
